transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... things have just gotten completely out of hand with my family. I know my in-laws aren't just having normal arguments with me anymore. It's gone way beyond that. They are actually using the altar and the parish committee at our church to push me out. They're trying to make everyone forget everything I have done for this family over the years. It's just... I can see exactly what they are doing, and I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
Aside from your concerns about your in-laws, have you been feeling unusually energized or, conversely, significantly down or hopeless lately?

Well, I wouldn't say I've felt down or hopeless. Not at all. But energized... yes, I suppose so. There were days recently when I just felt so bright and... completely certain about things. I had all this energy. 

But at the same time, if anyone questioned me about what was happening with the altar, I would just snap at them. I couldn't really help it. I'd get so angry, like they were insulting my whole family right to my face. So I guess my mood has been a bit all over the place in that way.
During the periods when you were feeling this way, were there any stretches of at least two weeks where you felt deeply sad, hopeless, or lost interest in almost all of your usual activities?

Yes, actually. After all that energy finally left me... well, things just dropped. For a while now, definitely a couple of weeks, I've been waking up with this heavy sadness. It just feels like... I don't know, like there is absolutely no joy left in my house anymore. Or in me, really.
Have these concerns about your in-laws and the church remained present even during the times when your mood felt more stable or normal?

Well, no, not exactly. The really extreme parts... like hearing voices and actually seeing my mother... that only happened during that time when I was barely sleeping. You know, when I was rushing around and feeling absolutely sure I had this special duty to fix the altar. 

Once all that energy went away and my mood dropped, I still felt guilty and sad, of course. But I wasn't hearing or seeing those things anymore. So they really just happened when I was all wound up.
During those weeks when you felt deeply sad and hopeless, did you continue to hold those firm beliefs about your in-laws and the church?

Yes, those thoughts definitely stayed with me. Actually, that's really why I came in to be seen in the first place. 

Even when I was feeling so down and all that energy was gone, I still knew my in-laws weren't just having a simple argument with me. It was much more than that. I knew they were using the altar, and getting the parish committee involved, just to push me out. It was like they were trying to make everyone forget everything I have done for this family. So, yes, even when I was sad, I still knew that was happening.

Looking back at the periods when you were not feeling particularly energized or particularly sad—the times when your mood felt more like your usual self—did you still hold those firm beliefs about your in-laws and the church?

No, not really. When I'm feeling normal, you know, just my regular self... I don't really think about it like that. I mean, we might still not get along, but I don't have those strong thoughts about them trying to push me out or using the church against me. That really only happens when I'm either feeling all wound up or really, really down. When I'm just regular, those thoughts aren't there.

Have you ever experienced these fixed beliefs about your in-laws or seen or heard things that weren't there at times when your mood was completely stable, outside of those periods where you felt either very high or very low?

No, not at all. Like I was saying a little bit ago, the voices and seeing my mother... that really only happened during that one time when I was barely sleeping and rushing around, when I was so sure I had that special duty to fix the altar. 

Once my mood dropped and I just felt sad and guilty, I wasn't hearing or seeing those things anymore. And when my mood is completely stable, just my regular self, I don't have those fixed thoughts about my in-laws, and I definitely don't see or hear anything that isn't there. It only happens when my mood is way up or way down.
